title: Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Secure Firewall Threat Defense Software Remote Access SSL VPN…
description:
This vulnerability affects Cisco devices if they are running a vulnerable release of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software or Cisco Secure FTD Software, the SSL remote access VPN login service is reachable, and secondary authentication is configured in the tunnel group scope that is described in the following sections.

For information about which Cisco software releases are vulnerable, see the Fixed Software ["#fs"] section of this advisory.
  Determine the SSL Remote Access VPN Configuration
If the running configuration contains the webvpn keyword and SSL VPN is enabled on at least one interface, the configuration is vulnerable, as shown in the following table:
        Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Secure FTD Software Feature  Vulnerable Configuration          SSL Remote Access VPN1
webvpn
enable <interface_name>

1. For Cisco Secure FTD Software, remote access VPN features are enabled from Devices > VPN > Remote Access in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) Software or from Remote Access VPN in Cisco Secure Firewall Device Manager (FDM).  Determine the Tunnel Group Configuration
If tunnel-group-list enable is configured, check all tunnel groups, including the default tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup, for secondary-authentication-server-group.

Note: This check is not limited to profiles that are displayed in the group list on the login page.

If tunnel-group-list enable is absent or has been removed using the no tunnel-group-list enable command, check the default tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup, for secondary-authentication-server-group because disabling the group list does not remove exposure when that default group uses secondary authentication.

Note: On Cisco Secure FTD Software, review the deployed remote access VPN policy and the resulting device running configuration in Cisco Secure FMC Software or Cisco Secure FDM. A successful VPN login is not required to reach the affected processing path.
